a man is a manservant or assistant; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A trivial scrap of verse survives from a poet whose helper has been sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest particle, as in 'not a whit', so a tiny insignificant bit.

clue.text: Sailor Jack eating a pie, drinking punch

parts.note: Little Jack Horner of the nursery rhyme sat in a corner eating his Christmas pie
a punch is a blow

explanation.surface: A seaman called Jack is snacking on pie while sipping a fruit punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a nickname for a sailor, but with 'eating a pie' it is the nursery-rhyme Jack Horner.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Hornblower is C. S. Forester's fictional naval officer, the most famous seafaring hero of the Napoleonic novels.

clue.text: Work of fantasy that man mails out in a vast quantity

indicators.note: in places the man and the jumbled letters inside the large number

indicators.note: out means the letters of mails are put out of order

explanation.surface: A man posts out a fantasy book in enormous numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a vast quantity' is not the definition, as the surface suggests; 'out' rearranges the mail, and 'in' sends the man and that jumble into the huge number just after its first letter, making SILMA from the five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's posthumous collection of myths of Middle-earth is a celebrated work of high fantasy.

clue.text: Distributor of the written word has Peter Wimsey perhaps stocked in various copies

indicators.note: stocked in means one piece is held inside the other, like goods kept in store

explanation.surface: A distributor of books keeps several editions of the Lord Peter Wimsey novels in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' jumbles the copies into POSICE; the aristocratic sleuth goes in after its third letter. 'Written word' suggests a publisher, but letters are written words too.
explanation.definitionFit: A post office handles letters and parcels, so it distributes written correspondence.

clue.text: I'm surprised Hercule Poirot initially covers up identity of his DumbWitness

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the assembled letters are read from the bottom, so backwards
covers means the two initials sit around the exclamation, one on each side
initially picks the first letter of each of the detective's two names

parts.note: coo is an exclamation of surprise, so it can stand for 'I'm surprised'

explanation.surface: Poirot gasps as he uncovers who the silent witness really is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives H and P, which 'covers' puts around COO to make HCOOP; 'up' turns that to read the other way. In Christie's Dumb Witness the title witness is Bob, a wire-haired terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The silent witness in Christie's novel is the terrier Bob, and a dog is colloquially a pooch.

clue.text: Unnamed person arranged tone poemswithout introductions

without introductions removes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'without introductions' drops T and P to leave ONE and OEMS; 'arranged' rearranges ONEOEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone means an unspecified person whose name is not given.

clue.text: "This writing business. Pencils and what-not. -, if you ask me. Silly stuff. Nothing in it." (Eeyore, Winnie-the-Pooh)

parts.note: open as an adjective, the word itself

explanation.definitionFit: Frances Trollope, mother of Anthony, wrote the travel book Domestic Manners of the Americans.

explanation.surface: Zorro's home stays concealed amid a recurring class war.
explanation.definitionFit: Casa is Spanish for house, and Zorro is a Spanish Californian nobleman, so his home is a casa.

clue.text: Openingof Ethan Frome rewritten by father without structure

indicators.note: by means set beside, here after the father

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

rewritten means the letters are set down again in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges E plus FROME into EEFORM. Ethan Frome is Edith Wharton's novella.

clue.text: Pass by James, who created a Christian church's part

an apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church

clue.text: Tale of criminality to stun bishop with progressive morals at first

explanation.walkthrough: Brighton Rock is Graham Greene's novel of gangland crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Greene's novel follows the teenage gangster Pinkie, a story of crime and sin.

clue.text: With howler corrected, it'sprofitable?

explanation.walkthrough: 'howler' looks like the thing being fixed, but its letters with WITH are what 'corrected' reworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthwhile repays the effort spent on it, so it is rewarding.

clue.text: Newspaper section covering USuniversity's undertaking

parts.note: the comment pages of a newspaper carry opinion pieces

explanation.definitionFit: A commitment is a pledge or promise, which is an undertaking.

clue.text: Gaudy Night's conclusion asTV series rendered empty

explanation.surface: The ending of Sayers's Gaudy Night is hollowed out when it becomes a television series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaudy Night' looks like the title, Sayers's Oxford novel, but Gaudy is the definition. TELE is the British colloquial word for television.

clue.text: Description of Herron's horses left in broadcast
